title: Site-perfect Hom formula and reversed Tor window in the intrinsic presentation
statement: For a prime l, a finite-dimensional extension E/Q_l, any scheme X, and a positive coefficient level n+1, let K and L be intrinsic pro-etale derived coefficient objects. If K is site-perfect, then RHom(K,A_X) tensor L is isomorphic to RHom(K,L), using the specified finiteIntrinsicClosed unit and tensor. For every Tor interval [a,b] for K and [c,d] for L, RHom(K,L) has Tor interval [c-b,d-a]. No geometric finite-type, constructibility or dimension assumptions are imposed. The notions are those of def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-site-perfect-complex and def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude.

source.place: First paragraph, site-perfect dual formula and sharper Tor interval.

proof.text: On the actual coefficient module-sheaf category install its existing sheafified tensor, closedness, Grothendieck abelianness, and functorial flat resolutions. For each derived object choose a representative and a K-flat augmentation. The native one-K-flat tensor comparison and the single-functor comparison identify its degree-zero tensor tests with those in HasProEtaleTorAmplitude. Conversely the same comparison transports each vanishing test to every representative and every allowed augmentation. Thus the recorded ordered Tor predicate is equivalent to the native derived torAmplitudeIn predicate together with its ordering condition.

Apply ringedSitePerfectDuality to K to obtain its perfect dual D, invertible bidual map, and natural evaluation isomorphism D tensor - to RHom(K,-) in the normalized model. Native closedAdjunction and uniqueness of left adjoints identify right tensor functors of the native model, the normalized duality model, and finiteIntrinsicClosed. Braiding identifies their left tensor functors. The right unitor of the duality model, this tensor comparison at the two units, and the intrinsic left unitor identify the intrinsic unit with the ordinary coefficient object. Applying RHom(K,-) to this unit isomorphism, then the tensor comparison and perfect evaluation, proves the first clause.

Apply perfect duality also to D, which is perfect by the first application. The evaluation isomorphisms and bidual isomorphism provide adjunctions (- tensor K) left adjoint to (D tensor -), and (- tensor D) left adjoint to (K tensor -), transported to native tensor by uniqueness of left adjoints. To prove that D tensor F[0] vanishes below -b, test maps from Y with Y vanishing above -b-1. The first adjunction turns them into maps Y tensor K to F[0]; the upper tensor bound for K and braiding put the source in degrees at most -1, namely IsLE(-1), so every such map is zero. To prove vanishing above -a, test maps to Y with Y vanishing below -a+1. The second adjunction turns them into maps F[0] to K tensor Y; the lower tensor bound puts the target in IsGE(1), so every such map is zero. T-structure orthogonality therefore gives the exact interval [-b,-a] for D. This is the adjunction proof of the source dual-Tor interval result, written directly so no construction of ExactPairing data is needed.

For any F in degree zero, the Tor interval of L places L tensor F[0] in degrees [c,d]. The upper and lower tensor bounds applied to D put D tensor (L tensor F[0]) in [-b+c,-a+d]. Associativity supplies the native Tor interval of D tensor L. The native closed adjunction and left-adjoint uniqueness identify this with the intrinsic tensor; transport the interval along perfect evaluation to RHom(K,L). Integer arithmetic identifies the endpoints with [c-b,d-a], and the two ordered input intervals imply the required output ordering. No nonempty site, constructibility, or geometric hypothesis enters the argument.

proof_origin.note: N3: direct Lean proof from existing perfect duality and native closed tensor. The Tor-window step is replaced by the adjunction and t-structure orthogonality argument of WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.DerivedCategory.FlatModel.torAmplitudeIn_of_exactPairing, with the two adjunctions obtained directly from perfect evaluation and biduality.

lean.statement:
theorem finiteIntrinsic_sitePerfect_hom_window
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E]
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (n : ℕ)
    (K L : proEtaleDerivedCategory X (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1)))
    (hK : IsFiniteCoefficientSitePerfect l E X n K) :
    Nonempty ((finiteIntrinsicDerivedTensor l E X n).obj
      ((finiteIntrinsicDerivedInternalHom l E X n).obj
        (op K, (finiteIntrinsicClosed l E X n).monoidal.tensorUnit), L) ≅
      (finiteIntrinsicDerivedInternalHom l E X n).obj (op K, L)) ∧
    ∀ a b c d : ℤ,
      HasProEtaleTorAmplitude X (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1)) K a b →
      HasProEtaleTorAmplitude X (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1)) L c d →
      HasProEtaleTorAmplitude X (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1))
        ((finiteIntrinsicDerivedInternalHom l E X n).obj (op K, L)) (c - b) (d - a)
